_comment: SKILL BLUEPRINT — output of the Spec agent, input to the Generator agent. One blueprint per standard.
subject: math
cluster: Apply and extend previous understandings of numbers to the system of rational numbers
description: Students order rational numbers (integers, fractions, and decimals, positive and negative) and reason about their relative position on the number line. They interpret inequality statements like $-3 > -7$ as statements about position, write inequalities to describe real-world situations, understand absolute value $|x|$ as a number's distance from $0$, interpret absolute value as magnitude in context (for example, account balance or temperature), and distinguish comparisons of order ($<,\,>$) from comparisons of absolute value (magnitude).
subSkills: Order a set of rational numbers from least to greatest (and greatest to least) on a number line
Write and interpret inequality statements such as $-8 < -5$ and explain them in terms of position on the number line
Translate a real-world description into an inequality (for example, a temperature warmer than $-3^{\circ}$C is $t > -3$)
Compute the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from $0$: $|-\tfrac{3}{4}| = \tfrac{3}{4}$
Interpret absolute value as magnitude in a real-world context (debt size, elevation below sea level, distance from a reference point)
Distinguish an order comparison ($a < b$) from an absolute-value (magnitude) comparison ($|a|$ vs $|b|$), recognizing that for negatives the larger absolute value is the smaller number

problemArchetypes.name: Interpret an inequality on the number line
problemArchetypes.example: Explain what $-6 < -1$ means about the positions of $-6$ and $-1$ on a number line.

problemArchetypes.name: Write an inequality from a context
problemArchetypes.example: An account is overdrawn when the balance is less than $\$0$. Write an inequality for a balance $b$ that is overdrawn.

problemArchetypes.name: Interpret absolute value as magnitude in context
problemArchetypes.example: Account A has a balance of $-\$30$ and account B has a balance of $-\$20$. Which account has the greater debt, and how does that relate to $|-30|$ and $|-20|$?

problemArchetypes.name: Order vs. absolute value comparison
problemArchetypes.example: Is the statement $-7 > -3$ true? Is $|-7| > |-3|$ true? Explain why the two answers differ.

Easy.description: Single-step recall and direct comparison with integers or simple values. Order two or three integers, read a true/false inequality, or compute the absolute value of an integer. No context interpretation required.
constraints: Values are integers or simple terminating decimals/halves, magnitudes $\le 10$
At most three numbers to order, or a single $|x|$ to compute
No real-world translation; symbols and numbers only

Medium.description: Mixed forms (fractions, decimals, and integers together) must be put on a common scale before ordering, or a short context must be turned into an inequality, or absolute value of a fraction/decimal is computed. Two related steps.
constraints: Mix at least two of: integers, fractions, decimals in one ordering task
Fractions/decimals with magnitudes that require conversion to compare
One context-to-inequality translation, or one $|x|$ with $x$ a fraction or decimal

Hard.description: Multi-step reasoning that combines order and magnitude: compare numbers that look counterintuitive because of sign, justify why a larger absolute value can be the smaller number, or interpret absolute value as magnitude inside a real-world comparison and answer a follow-up.
constraints: Requires distinguishing order ($<,>$) from absolute value in the same problem
Includes negatives where the larger magnitude is the smaller number
Real-world interpretation plus a justification or follow-up comparison

difficultyRubric.tierSplit: If split into two worksheets: tier1 covers ordering and basic absolute-value computation (Easy to Medium); tier2 covers context translation and the order-vs-magnitude distinction (Medium to Hard), with no item overlap.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student orders negatives by magnitude, treating the number with the larger digits as larger
Student thinks absolute value just removes (or flips) the sign rather than giving distance from zero, applying it inconsistently
commonMisconceptions.distractor: Writes $|-5| = -5$ (keeps the negative) or $|3| = -3$ (adds a negative)

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student confuses order with absolute value, asserting the smaller number always has the smaller absolute value
commonMisconceptions.distractor: Says that because $-30 < -20$, the debt of $\$20$ is greater, instead of $|-30| > |-20|$ so $\$30$ is the greater debt

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student reverses the inequality symbol when translating a context with negatives
commonMisconceptions.distractor: Writes $b > 0$ for an overdrawn (below zero) balance instead of $b < 0$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student fails to convert to a common form, comparing fractions and decimals by raw digits
commonMisconceptions.distractor: Orders $\frac{1}{4}$ as greater than $0.75$ because $4 > 0.75$ is read off the denominator

_comment_itemCounts: worksheet.single = one ramped sheet (Easy->Hard across 15 items). tier1/tier2 only used if the standard is split into two worksheets.
